alley.name: The Alley Behind the Mistletoe Lounge

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The North Pole. Christmas Eve. Snow coming down like it had somewhere better to be.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The name's Tiny Hightower. Private investigator. I see this town from knee level, and believe me, it doesn't look any better from down here.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: My office is a broom closet off the third floor hallway. The broom still lives here. We don't talk.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I was four hot cocoas deep when trouble came knocking. Trouble usually knocks at my height. This trouble knocked way up high.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Hello? Is this the detective? The sign on the door said detective.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The sign was right, ma'am. Down here.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Oh! Oh, my. I've been talking to your coat rack.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Happens a lot. The coat rack's solved two cases.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: She was leaving a little puddle everywhere she stood. Old snow does that.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I made a mental note to forget it.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: It's my son, Jimmy. He sings at the Mistletoe Lounge. He didn't come home last night.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: He calls himself Jimmy Mittens now. For show business. His real name is Jimmy Slush, like his father, may he rest in the freezer.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A stage name. Every crooner's got one. Every crooner's also got enemies.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: I told him he had a snowball's chance in hell in show business. He never listened.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I weighed my options. I could take the case. I could take the case. Or, and hear me out, I could take the case.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: It was agonizing. I took the case.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The bottom drawer. The only drawer I can reach. Inside, my most trusted instrument.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Tinsel goggles. Military grade. Okay, party grade. But they see things the naked eye can't.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Mostly sparkles. But also things.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Do you need a lift, dear? Or a ride? Or a step stool?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I'll take the stairs, ma'am. All forty of them. Each one up to my chin.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Outside, the snow was falling sideways, like it was trying to leave town too.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The Mistletoe Lounge was six blocks away. For a regular guy, that's a stroll. For me, that's a pilgrimage.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: I'm coming with you. Jimmy's my boy.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: It could get dangerous, ma'am.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Dear, I'm eighty-seven and made of snow. Everything is dangerous.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Two paths lay before me. Walk six blocks. Or take the bus.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Walking meant freedom. The bus meant a seat. I ran the numbers. Then I ran them again. Then I lost count.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I took the bus. A man's gotta know his limits. Mine are about three feet.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The bus stop. Where this city's lost souls wait for the eleven fifteen that always shows up at eleven forty.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The bus pulled up. The first step came up to my eyebrows.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Up you go, dear. My, you had a snowball's chance in hell with that step.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: We rode in silence. The city slid past the window. Six blocks. The longest six blocks of my life.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Around block three, I questioned everything. By block four, I had answers. By block five, I'd forgotten them.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Block six. Our stop. Granny pulled the cord. I pointed at it with authority.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The alley behind the Mistletoe Lounge. The band was still playing Jimmy's song through the wall, like nothing happened.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Police tape. A gingerbread cop. And a lady reindeer, warm as a July sidewalk, chatting up a snowman by the dumpster.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Just another night in the big icy.

lines.speaker: sgt_snap
lines.text: Whoa, whoa. Crime scene. No civilians. Sergeant Snap, North Pole PD.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Tiny Hightower. Private.

lines.speaker: sgt_snap
lines.text: Private what? Where are you even... oh. Down there.

lines.speaker: sgt_snap
lines.text: Look, pal, it's open and shut. Snowman goes out, snowman doesn't come back. Happens every spring.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: It's December, sergeant.

lines.speaker: sgt_snap
lines.text: Don't push me, pal. I'm already crumbling under the pressure. Literally. That was my elbow.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: There he was. Or there he wasn't. A top hat. A scarf. A carrot. Two lumps of coal, staring up at me.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Oh, Jimmy. My poor baby. You always did spread yourself too thin.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A puddle. Could mean anything. Rain. A spilled drink. A very sad cloud.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I wasn't ruling anything out. Except the obvious. I always rule out the obvious. It's too obvious.

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Well, hello there, little man. Somebody call a detective?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: From down here, all I could see of her were her hooves. They were on fire. Probably a fashion thing.

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: I'm Comet. Poor Jimmy. We were... acquainted. He was a real cool guy. Before.

lines.speaker: lil_sleet
lines.text: H-hi. I'm Lil' Sleet. Big fan of Jimmy's. Is it hot out here, or is it just me?

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: It's just you, sugar.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The kid was sweating bullets. Big, wet, drippy bullets. Nerves, probably. Murder does that to people.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Something about this alley didn't add up. Time for the goggles.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: With the tinsel goggles on, the alley lit up like a department store window.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Scorch marks. Shaped like hooves. A trail of them, leading up to the puddle, and then over to the dumpster.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Somebody'd been having a barbecue back here. In a blizzard. The plot thickened, like gravy.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: And up on the wall, way out of reach, something was smoking.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Hold still, dear. Up we go. Oof. You had a snowball's chance in hell of reaching that on your own.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Up close, I saw it. A lipstick kiss on the brick, right about where a snowman's face would be. Still smoking.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Warm to the touch. Very warm. Ow.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Whoever kissed Jimmy last left their mark. And then they left him a puddle.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I had a theory. A big one. I'd tell you, but I'm saving it.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Well? Do you know who did this to my Jimmy?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I have several leads, ma'am. All of them point inside that lounge. One of them points at the dumpster.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Find who did this. Or I'll find a detective who can reach the doorbell.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I looked up at the Mistletoe Lounge. Way, way up. Somewhere in there was a killer. And hopefully a step stool.
